response.sql: WITH city_counts AS (SELECT city_id, COUNT(*) AS address_count FROM address GROUP BY city_id), total AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM address), ranked AS (SELECT c.city_id, c.address_count, CAST(c.address_count AS DOUBLE) / t.n AS fraction, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY c.address_count DESC) AS rnk FROM city_counts c CROSS JOIN total t) SELECT city_id, address_count, fraction FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY fraction DESC, city_id

assumptions.assumption: The target is MySQL 8.0 or later, since the schema is Sakila-style MySQL and the query uses CTEs and RANK() window functions.
The top-10 cutoff uses RANK() on address count, so every city tied with the 10th-place count is included and the result may have more than 10 rows.
The denominator is the total row count of the address table. Every address has a non-null city_id, so no addresses are excluded from the total.

The fraction is computed as a DOUBLE to avoid MySQL's default decimal division precision. Cities with equal fractions are ordered by city_id ascending so the output is deterministic; the request does not specify this tie-break.
